We need to extract explicit facts.

Text: "Catalan language

Western Catalan comprises the two dialects of Northwestern Catalan and Valencian; the Eastern block comprises four dialects: Central Catalan, Balearic, Rossellonese, and Alguerese. Each dialect can be further subdivided in several subdialects."

We need triplets.

Subject: Western Catalan (type maybe language variety). Relation: comprises (or "has part")? In Wikidata style, relation could be "has part" or "includes". Use "has part". Object: Northwestern Catalan (type dialect) and Valencian (dialect). Since two objects, we split into two triplets.

Similarly, Eastern block comprises four dialects: Central Catalan, Balearic, Rossellonese, Alguerese. So subject: Eastern block (type maybe language block). Relation: has part. Objects each.

Also "Catalan language" maybe subject? Not needed.

Also "Each dialect can be further subdivided in several subdialects." That's a generic statement, not specific entities. Might be expressed as relation: "has subdialect" with object "subdialect" but not specific. Probably not extract because no explicit named subdialects.

Thus produce triplets:

1. subject "Western Catalan", relation "has part", object "Northwestern Catalan". qualifiers none. subject_type "language variety", object_type "dialect".

2. subject "Western Catalan", relation "has part", object "Valencian". same types.

3. subject "Eastern block", relation "has part", object "Central Catalan". subject_type "language block", object_type "dialect".

4. subject "Eastern block", relation "has part", object "Balearic". same.

5. subject "Eastern block", relation "has part", object "Rossellonese". same.

6. subject "Eastern block", relation "has part", object "Alguerese". same.

Potential also "Catalan language" maybe parent of Western Catalan and Eastern block? Not stated explicitly. So not.
